title: Predictive Maintenance for Pharmaceutical Equipment
short: Uses sensor and maintenance history to predict equipment failures before they stop a batch.
symptom: Machines fail in the middle of a batch
ingredient: A failure early-warning for critical equipment
directions: Connect equipment sensor data and maintenance logs. Engineering receives risk scores and suggested inspection windows.
problem: Tablet presses, coaters, filling lines and HVAC units are maintained on fixed schedules; unexpected failures still interrupt batches and trigger deviations.
why: An unplanned stop can mean a rejected batch, an investigation, lost capacity and supply delays.
solution: Learns normal operating patterns from vibration, temperature, pressure and current signals, detects drift toward failure and suggests when to inspect — fitting maintenance into planned downtime.
data: Sensor time series (vibration, temperature, pressure, power)
limitations: Needs months of sensor data including some failures
Changes to qualified equipment follow change control
review: Maintenance engineers decide on every intervention; qualified-state changes go through change control.
